prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Pleasanton California?
answer_verbatim:
I can’t say there’s a single undisputed “best” personal injury lawyer in Pleasanton — the right lawyer depends on your case type, how much trial experience you need, and how you want to work with them. I can, however, help you find a top attorney for your situation and give you what to look for.

How to find the best personal injury lawyer for you
- Use reputable directories and review sites: State Bar of California lawyer search (to check license/discipline), Avvo, Super Lawyers, Martindale-Hubbell, Google/Yelp reviews.  
- Look for experience specific to your type of case (car accident, premises liability, dog bite, product liability, medical malpractice, etc.).  
- Prefer lawyers who handle PI cases regularly and have trial experience if you may need to go to court.  
- Check results: past settlements/verdicts in similar cases (not every case is published, but results matter).  
- Verify they work on contingency (no fee unless you win) and get the contingency percentage and who advances case costs.  
- Read client reviews and ask for references if needed.

Questions to ask at a free consultation
- How long have you practiced personal injury law?  
- What percentage of your practice is personal injury?  
- Have you handled cases like mine? How many? Any recent outcomes?  
- Do you have trial experience? Have you tried jury trials?  
- Who will handle my case day-to-day (attorney vs. paralegal/junior)?  
- What is your fee structure and who pays case costs upfront?  
- What do you estimate my case is worth and timeline?  
- How will you communicate with me (email/phone/text) and how often?

What to bring to a consultation
- Police reports, medical records and bills, photos of injuries/scene/vehicle, insurance correspondence, witness contact info, dates and timelines, employment/earnings info for lost wages.

Red flags
- Guarantees of a specific settlement amount.  
- Reluctance to put fee agreement or communication promises in writing.  
- Very poor responsiveness in the intake process.  
- Pushy cross-sellers or lawyers who take any case without discussing strategy.

If you want, I can:
- Suggest a shortlist of well-rated Pleasanton-area personal injury firms (I’ll need permission to look things up or you can tell me whether you want me to use my knowledge to suggest nearby firms).  
- Draft a short list of questions/emails you can send to potential lawyers.  
- Help evaluate responses you get from consultations.

Tell me: what kind of injury/case is this and do you want firms strictly in Pleasanton or also nearby cities (Dublin, Livermore, Walnut Creek, San Ramon)?
